reading.body:
The Weaver's classification as a data center cannot be confirmed. OpenStreetMap tags it as telecom=data_center, but the name suggests a textile business, craft operation, or hospitality venue rather than IT infrastructure. Research to verify the tag was incomplete due to tool limitations.

This entry illustrates a broader problem in mapping AI infrastructure: public databases sometimes misclassify facilities, and confirming actual data-center use requires resources beyond automated tagging. A name like "The Weaver" provides no positive signal toward computing operations. Without business registration details, operator information, or power draw data, the distinction between a genuine facility and a mistagged premises cannot be made.

The record does not disclose capacity, power consumption, or operational status. Its location near Alicante airport is noted, but proximity alone does not indicate infrastructure quality or suitability for AI workloads. This case demonstrates why facility-level power and compute data, rather than names and location tags, must anchor any accounting of AI infrastructure growth.
